summary: A handled alert stays handled until its condition actually clears, with critical exempt

coordination.notes: The design says a Set of handled keys; this uses a Map of the retired alerts, because the point of keeping the record is occurrences - 'stunned four rounds running' is worth more than 'stunned', and a Set would discard it at the moment it starts to matter. reconcile takes the keys deriveAlerts produced this pass, so what counts as still-true stays with the code that decides what an alert is. One pre-existing check had to change: 'the same key can be raised again later as a new alert' asserted deduplicated === false and occurrences === 1, which was the mechanism, while its name states the property. The property is now more true, not less - the key becomes actionable again and preempts - so the body was rewritten to assert that, and the commit says so, because editing a test to make your own change pass is indistinguishable from this unless it is named.

checks: 'OK the same condition next round does not re-enter the queue  0', 'OK but it is still counted, because four rounds stunned is worth more than one  2'
'OK reconcile forgets a handled condition that is no longer reported  situation:stunned', 'OK a condition that ended and came back is a fresh alert  1'
